name: Priya Rahman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, independent of AI firms, employers, unions, political parties and government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What happens during your ordinary shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the morning chat team at a contact centre and take the disputed travel bookings that have already bounced between agents. I studied for a two-year college diploma and I am good at finding a broken rule in a long account. I use the approved AI assistant every day to sort old messages, then check dates and amounts myself. The pay for this lead job is lower than it should be.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband Tariq repairs bicycles, and our children are six and eleven. We have a mortgage and three weeks of expenses saved; repairs to the roof took the rest. Only a few similar centres are close enough for our school routine. I like a useful tool, but a mortgage lender does not pay us for being curious.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team the assistant is a good filing clerk, not a referee. A booking credit still needs a human to check the journey date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would like a quiet year because my lead pay is low and the roof bill emptied most of our savings. A small time saving will not fix that, though my shifts should stay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep handling the disputed bookings and checking AI drafts against the live account. Starting now, I will send a small fixed amount from each pay into the roof reserve; in the first year I will put off repainting the kitchen until we have one mortgage payment saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about money, even if work carries on. The ceiling is dry, but the bank balance is thinner than the plaster.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does the assistant miss?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It once mixed a cancelled train with a trip the customer actually took. I caught it because the payment date sat on the next page of the account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Tariq agree about the kitchen?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My husband Tariq would, although he has already bought colour samples. We can live with the old paint longer than we can live without a mortgage payment.

say: I would call AI a **filing clerk**, not the final judge.
I would keep a **journey-date check** on booking credits.
think: I expect my **morning shifts** to hold because small AI shortcuts leave disputed bookings with my team.
I know low pay and **roof costs** leave us vulnerable anyway.
do: Keep resolving **booking disputes** and checking live dates.
Save from each pay toward a **roof reserve** before repainting.
S0.quote: The ceiling is dry, but the bank balance is thinner than the plaster.
fieldNote: She uses **approved AI daily** but checks its answers.
Roof repairs left only **three weeks saved**.
The postponed **kitchen paint** has a clear mortgage reason.

steps.text: Keep resolving disputed travel bookings and checking AI drafts against live accounts
Save a fixed amount from each pay toward one mortgage payment
Delay repainting the kitchen until one mortgage payment is saved

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell agents to measure the bookings customers reopen after AI closes them. Faster replies are useful only when the credit reaches the right account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can learn the new controls quickly, but I could still lose paid hours if most routine chats vanish. Tariq has workshop work, yet his wage will not carry our mortgage and the children alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will test the approved assistant on thirty closed booking disputes and learn its new review screen with the quality lead during paid shifts. I will take error counts to the manager myself and ask for time to correct AI mistakes. If my rota falls in the first year, I will apply for posted paid review work only where written wages and hours cover our mortgage and school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious about the rota. Knowing the tool makes me useful, but it cannot guarantee a full week of pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you leave for another centre?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: There are only a few nearby, so I would compare actual vacancies before changing anything. I will not leave my current wage for a promise of a quality title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the new screen teach you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It shows which account evidence the assistant used. I want to learn where that evidence goes stale before I sign a correction.

say: I would count **reopened bookings** after automated replies.
I would ask for **correction time** backed by error counts.
think: I can learn **review controls** quickly because I already check live accounts against AI drafts each day.
I still fear **paid-hour cuts** that Tariq’s wage cannot cover.
do: Test **thirty closed disputes** and learn the AI review screen on paid shifts.
Ask the manager for **correction time** using error counts.
Apply after rota cuts only for **posted paid review** with written mortgage-covering wages, hours and pickup.
S1.quote: I will not leave my current wage for a promise of a quality title.
fieldNote: Her AI learning is an **actual paid-shift test**, beyond routine use.
She takes the **manager request herself**, not as worker group action.
Few local vacancies limit even an **adaptive** agent.

steps.text: Test thirty closed bookings and learn AI review screen during paid shifts
Apply after cuts for posted paid review with written mortgage-covering wages, hours and school pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that full thinking AI by 2028 could do nearly all our booking chats. Robots around 2031 do not buy a screen job three more years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my lead post could end even if I am the best at the current system. Three weeks of savings is frighteningly short, and Tariq cannot cover the mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask the employer for written dates and put our kitchen work on hold. I will ask my sister Leila whether we could share school pickup if I need a longer commute. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I will apply outside contact centres only for posted paid clinic reception roles with written mortgage-covering wages and hours; I will not resign before an offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am alarmed. The date is so near that a new tool might arrive before the roof fund recovers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why clinic reception?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I already untangle booking errors, but a clinic has different records and rules. I would need to see a real paid opening and the shift pattern before calling it an option.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a course now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would complete a required privacy course if a posted clinic vacancy funded it and paid my time. I will not spend the remaining roof money on a certificate without a job attached.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** threatens booking chats.
I would separate **2031 robots** from the earlier screen risk.
think: I expect my **lead post** might end even though I am good at the present booking system.
Our **three-week reserve** cannot bridge a long search.
do: Request **written dates**, delay kitchen work and ask Leila whether she can share pickup if a longer commute becomes necessary.
Complete **required privacy training** only for a posted clinic vacancy funding fees and paid time.
Apply outside centres after job loss for **posted paid clinic reception** with written mortgage-covering wages/hours; do not resign before an offer.
feel: **Alarmed** by the short clock and tiny reserve.
S2.quote: I will not spend the remaining roof money on a certificate without a job attached.
fieldNote: The **clinic route** requires a posted paid opening and written wage.
She will not resign before a **written offer** covering mortgage and hours.
She asks whether her sister **could share pickup**; no help is promised.

steps.text: Delay kitchen work while protecting the remaining roof money
Ask sister Leila about school pickup for a longer commute
Complete required privacy course only for posted clinic role funding fees and paid time
Move after job loss only on written paid clinic offer covering mortgage, hours and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years lets us check whether review jobs actually appear. Our booking chats still face general AI in 2031, with hands-on robots following around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could build a second skill while my current wage still arrives, but I cannot buy a future job. We have a mortgage and three weeks saved, not a fund for open-ended study.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep the morning team and ask the quality department for a paid shadow shift each month. If it posts a paid audit vacancy with wages and hours covering our mortgage and school pickup, and funds the required audit course on paid time, I will complete it. In the first year after 2031 I will move only after a written offer with those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, though I can do more with five years than two. I want to see someone actually earning the review wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the shadow shift show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would watch how an auditor checks an AI decision against the booking ledger. If the department cannot spare a paid shift, I will learn from the complaints I already handle.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Tariq change work at the same time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, we would keep his bicycle workshop wage if possible while I tested the new role. We cannot put both household wages at risk in the same month.

say: I would ask whether **paid audit roles** appear before 2031.
I would note **2034 robots** come after screen work changes.
think: I can build **audit skill** while current wages arrive.
I cannot fund **open-ended study** from three weeks saved.
do: Keep my **morning team**; request monthly paid quality shadowing and use current cases if no paid shift is available.
Complete **funded required audit training** on paid time only for a posted paid vacancy with mortgage-covering wages, hours and workable pickup.
Move after 2031 only on a **written offer** meeting those terms; retain Tariq’s workshop wage if possible.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect a real wage.
S3.quote: We cannot put both household wages at risk in the same month.
fieldNote: The **shadow shift** is paid or she learns from current cases.
The **audit course** needs a vacancy, funded fees and paid time.
Tariq’s **workshop wage** should continue during her move if possible.

steps.text: Keep leading paid morning booking shifts and request monthly paid audit shadowing
Complete funded audit course on paid time only for posted role covering mortgage and pickup
Move on written offer with mortgage-covering wages, hours, pickup, and Tariq's wage if possible

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team a decade is time to find paid work beyond chat windows, not a reason to stop checking them. General AI reaches desks in 2036; hands-on robots arrive around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I might still have a mortgage, but the children should be older. I would like a full year of expenses before either adult takes a risky move, built from wages rather than borrowing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep my lead shift and transfer a fixed share of pay to the roof reserve. Twice a year I will check posted quality and clinic roles and their full rotas. If my call hours fall in the first year after 2036, I will move only on a written paid offer with wages and hours covering the mortgage, while Tariq keeps his workshop wage if possible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about that endpoint, but the time gives us a chance to fill the savings jar. Curiosity is easier to use when the mortgage payment is already safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the savings goal slips?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If either wage drops, the one-year target moves back. I will not borrow to make the balance look better.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our children that a job title is not dinner. We compare the hours, the journey and who picks them up before either of us signs anything.

say: I would compare **posted paid roles** over the decade.
I would separate **2036 desk risk** from 2039 robots.
think: I want **one year saved** before a risky move.
I know the **mortgage** may still be due at 53.
do: Keep my **lead shift** and save a fixed pay share toward one year before risky moves; accept delays if wages fall.
Check **posted roles** and full rotas twice yearly.
Move after cuts only on **written paid mortgage-covering wages/hours** with workable pickup; retain Tariq’s wage if possible.
S4.quote: Curiosity is easier to use when the mortgage payment is already safe.
fieldNote: Her **one-year target** moves back if either wage falls.
She checks **full rotas** rather than titles.
Tariq’s **current wage** should stay during her move if possible.

steps.text: Keep leading paid morning booking shifts
Save pay toward one year before risky moves; delay target if wages fall
Move after cuts on written mortgage-covering wages/hours with workable pickup; retain Tariq’s wage if possible
Compare journeys, pickup and both rotas before either signs a new offer

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. A good test score will not pay a mortgage if the whole chat team goes. Written notice, a posted paid job and funded training on paid time would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who has authority to reopen a booking the machine marks settled. The wrong credit lands in a real household account. Somebody needs paid time to put it right.

headlineQuote: The wrong credit lands in a real household account.
portrait: Priya is a **43-year-old team lead** with a two-year diploma and strong booking skill.
She uses **approved AI daily** and experiments early, while checking live records herself.
Low pay, a **mortgage and children**, three weeks saved and few nearby centres keep her choices narrow.
She seeks **paid audit experience** and moves only for posted work with written household-covering terms.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her chat wage before roof savings recover.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, posted paid work and funded training on paid time would help.
